question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?
explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are the foundational pillars of public health messaging and community health promotion. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is communication in IEC a two-way process rather than a one-way lecture?

options.A: It is required by government policy for every primary health center.
options.B: It ensures that nurses do not have to speak during health outreaches.
options.C: It allows healthcare providers to listen to community fears and local beliefs.
options.D: It stops patients from asking difficult questions about medications.

explanation: Great nursing is all about listening, not just talking! Two-way communication helps us understand what people are really going through so we can help better. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do a community diagnosis before starting an IEC campaign?

options.A: Identify the actual health burdens affecting the local population
options.B: Prove that the community lacks basic hygiene practices
options.C: Fulfill administrative paperwork requirements for the local government
options.D: Determine how many nurses are needed for night duty shifts

explanation: You got it! Just like assessing an individual patient before treatment, a community diagnosis helps you find out what health issues are truly troubling the people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h2)

question: A nurse checks clinic attendance registers to see which illnesses bring patients in most often. What is this called?
explanation: Spot on! Looking at clinic records to track disease patterns is a classic way we gather epidemiological data to plan our next steps. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is the main goal of Behavior Change Communication (BCC)?

options.A: Replacing traditional healers with modern doctors
options.B: Ensuring every household buys expensive water filters
options.C: Helping people adopt and sustain healthy lifestyle practices
options.D: Increasing the number of patients admitted to hospital wards

explanation: Exactly! BCC goes beyond just sharing facts; it's about helping people make real, lasting changes that keep them healthy. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why might someone know a health practice is dangerous yet continue doing it?

options.A: They enjoy being sick and visiting the primary health clinic
options.B: Nurses failed to write down the instructions on a chalkboard
options.C: Government laws forbid them from changing their personal habits
options.D: Economic, social, or cultural barriers make the healthy choice difficult

explanation: So true! Knowing what to do is only half the battle. Money, culture, and daily struggles often make healthy choices tough to practice. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which IEC channel works best for reaching a scattered rural population quickly?
explanation: Correct! Radio is a powerful tool because it travels far and wide, reaching people in remote areas in no time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a major downside of relying only on text-heavy pamphlets in a rural community?

options.A: They take too long to read during a surgical procedure.
options.B: They are too expensive for the federal government to print.
options.C: They are ineffective for community members with low literacy levels.
options.D: They encourage people to ignore traditional folk songs.

explanation: Spot on! If people cannot read easily, text-heavy flyers won't help. That's why pictures, radio, and drama are often much better choices. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h4)

question: Who should you talk to first when introducing a new health program to a traditional community?

options.A: Newly graduated nursing students from the city
options.B: Commercial transport drivers in the motor park
options.C: International donor agencies and foreign embassies

explanation: You got it! Respecting elders and local leaders opens the door for the community to trust and accept your health program. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is community ownership so important for the long-term success of health projects?

options.A: It guarantees that the clinic will make a profit from drug sales.
options.B: It removes all responsibilities from the shoulders of community nurses.
options.C: Locals will sustain and protect the program after external support ends.
options.D: Government health budgets will no longer be needed at all.

explanation: Exactly! When the community feels the project is theirs, they will keep it running strong long after outsiders pack up and leave. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main difference between monitoring and evaluation in a project?

options.A: Monitoring happens after the project ends, while evaluation happens before it starts.
options.B: Monitoring deals with money, while evaluation deals strictly with medicines.
options.C: Monitoring is done by the community, while evaluation is done by politicians.
options.D: Monitoring tracks activities during implementation, while evaluation measures final impact.

explanation: Spot on! Monitoring is what you do while the work is going on, while evaluation checks the final results after everything is done. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)

question: A nurse wants to make sure new health posters are clear before printing thousands of copies. What should she do?

options.A: Ask doctors in the capital city to review the picture quality
options.B: Distribute all the posters immediately to save transport costs
options.C: Pre-test the posters with a small group of local community members
options.D: Translate the medical text into Latin for a more professional look

explanation: Brilliant! Always pre-test your materials with the target audience first to catch confusing pictures or messages before mass printing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h6)
